title.orig: Aedh Wishes for the Cloths of Heaven
title.en: He Wishes for the Cloths of Heaven
title.zh: 他希望得到天国的锦缎

edition.en: The Wind Among the Reeds (1899), on Project Gutenberg (eBook 32233), where it is titled “Aedh Wishes for the Cloths of Heaven”
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 32233 所录《苇间风》（1899），题作《艾德希望得到天国的锦缎》

basis.en: First published in 1899; the author died in 1939.
basis.zh: 1899 年首次发表；作者卒于 1939 年。

note.en: In The Wind Among the Reeds it was “Aedh Wishes for the Cloths of Heaven”; Yeats renamed it later. Eight lines built from a few repeated words: cloths, light, feet, dreams. The last line asks for care from anyone who is handed something fragile, which is also a fair thing to ask of a library’s readers.
note.zh: 在《苇间风》里，它题为《艾德希望得到天国的锦缎》；叶芝后来改了名。八行诗用几个反复出现的词搭成：锦缎、光、脚、梦。最后一行请求每一个接过易碎之物的人小心对待——对一座图书馆的读者，这也是一个合理的请求。

excerpt.orig:
I have spread my dreams under your feet;
Tread softly because you tread on my dreams.
excerpt.en:
I have spread my dreams under your feet;
Tread softly because you tread on my dreams.
excerpt.zh:
我已把我的梦铺在你的脚下；
轻一点踩吧，因为你踩着的是我的梦。
